label: original-phase, mid-sequence (t=2..6) step after a prefix opening with f/s/j/z/v/r/1/3/n/h, on a token outside that set
explanation: Almost only fires in the original-input phase (98.8% of mass), never at t=0-1, peaking at t=3-5 and dying out by t=8; it is essentially silent in the copy phase, with a small tail at the <DEL> step. It looks like a distributed, weighted read of the prefix: it is strongest when the earliest tokens come from a set A = {f,s,j,z,v,r,1,3,n,h} (first_tok f gives 7.3x lift, s/r/1 about 3x) and the current input is a first occurrence of a token outside A, especially w (5.8x), o, 0, t, c, a, e. The top activations (~0.3) are on w right after a run of A tokens, e.g. f n f z v [w]. Requiring both orig(0) and orig(1) in A, a non-A current token, and t=2..6 captures about 64% of activation mass, but precision is only about 25%: many such steps stay silent, and some activations follow prefixes with only one A token. Adding a whitelist for the current token raises precision to about 35% but lowers recall. Magnitude goes up with how strongly the prefix is made of A tokens and with the identity of the current token (w highest). This is not a clean monosemantic description.
